chapter: Chez Florence, the Hot Club and Django
title: The Stage B cabaret band with Django Reinhardt
summary: As a partner in a Montparnasse cabaret, Briggs hired Django Reinhardt, George Marion, Alix Combelle and Stephane Grappelli, whose rest-hour guitar-and-violin sets grew into a quintet.

bands.name: Quintette du Hot Club de France

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Let's go back then, just a little bit still. It was interesting what you were saying to me before, about how Django got into all this.
Yes, yes.
Playing in the Montparnasse. We had the Hot Club of France.
Right.
But you see, it was a night -- it was around -- no, it doesn't really make any difference, all comes to coincide, because they were short periods.
Right.
Django -- I was an
Briggs

associate of --, a business partner -- I'm mixing French and everything else -- a business partner at the Stage B -- MR. COLLIER: Which was? MR. BRIGGS: A cabaret in Montparnasse, on Boulevard Montparnasse. On the Left Bank. I -- in order to form the orchestra, I engaged Django Reinhardt, George Marion on drums, Alix Combelle on tenor-sax -- he was only learning the saxophone at the time -- and Stephane Grapelly on piano-violin. Well, it so happened that in order for us to get a rest in the evening, especially after 1:00 o'clock, Grapelly would play his violin and Django would play his guitar. And often, his brother would be there, Joseph, would be there, and we had two guitars and a violin, and it sounded pretty good then. Vola would come in, Vola, contra-
Briggs

bass, and the basses, would come in -- or some other bass player would come in, and then you had a quartet. You just needed another guitar, or one of the other gypsies would come in and you had a quintet. That's how it happened.
Vola is Louis Vola, is that right?
Louis Vola.
He was a bandleader. He had his own band?
He had his own band. He had his own band at that time. At the time he was working with a saxophone player by the name of Ekyan -- have you heard of him?
Yeh.
He was working at the Cor du Sud, with Ekyan, and I believe Al Romain -- you know Al Romain, the piano player?
Briggs 301
No, no.
He's actually at the Hilton Hotel. He's a personal friend 'cause he's one of the oldtimers, a little younger, but -- and Al Romain was at the Cor du Sud with Ekyan.
That was on the Left Bank too?
That was the Left Bank, yes, the Left Bank, further down from where I was.
And they got -- I think they had the band together, Al Romain and Andre Ekyan, they had the band together.
